root_cause_summary: The module correctly derives internal write/read qualifiers wr_valid (=wr_cs&&wr_en&&!full) and rd_valid (=rd_cs&&rd_en&&!empty) and uses them to gate wr_pointer/rd_pointer/status_cnt updates, but the physical dual-port RAM instantiation bypasses these qualifiers: we_0 is driven directly from raw wr_en (not wr_valid) and oe_1 is driven directly from raw rd_en (not rd_valid). This lets the RAM perform a real write even when the FIFO is full (silently corrupting the oldest un-read entry at wr_pointer, which is about to be read next) or drive stale/garbage read data when the FIFO is empty, desynchronizing the actual RAM contents from the counted occupancy (status_cnt) that the empty/full flags are derived from.
expected_behavior: Per REQ-002, the design must add internal write/read qualification so that the FIFO 'cannot silently overflow or underflow even if wr_en/rd_en are asserted when the FIFO is already full/empty.' This protection must apply to the actual RAM write/read enables, not merely to the pointer/counter update logic.
observed_behavior: UVM log shows empty asserted while COUNT>0 (55ns, 65ns), followed by reads returning 0x0/stale data (75ns, 85ns), and a simultaneous write/read mismatch returning the previous read's data (135ns) and a late read mismatch at 2765ns returning stale data — consistent with RAM contents being corrupted or stale relative to the counted occupancy tracked by status_cnt.
reasoning: wr_valid and rd_valid are computed specifically to prevent illegal writes/reads from disturbing FIFO state, but they are only wired to the pointer/counter update logic, not to the RAM's we_0/oe_1 ports. This means an illegal write (wr_cs&&wr_en while full) still physically executes in the RAM at the current wr_pointer address — an address holding valid, not-yet-read data — silently corrupting it without any pointer/counter change, so status_cnt still correctly tracks occupancy but the RAM data returned on a later legitimate read is wrong/stale, producing exactly the READ FAIL / stale-data / simultaneous WR-RD mismatch pattern seen in the log. Gating we_0 with wr_valid (which already includes !full) and oe_1 with rd_valid (which already includes !empty) closes this gap, ensuring RAM state changes stay perfectly synchronized with the qualified operations that update status_cnt/pointers, per REQ-002's explicit overflow/underflow protection requirement.
patch:
--- a/projects/fifo/rtl/syn_fifo.sv
+++ b/projects/fifo/rtl/syn_fifo.sv
@@
 ram_dp_ar_aw #(DATA_WIDTH,ADDR_WIDTH) DP_RAM (
   .clk     (clk),
 .address_0 (wr_pointer) , // address_0 input
 .data_0    (data_in)    , // data_0 bi-directional
 .cs_0      (wr_cs)      , // chip select
-.we_0      (wr_en)      , // write enable
+.we_0      (wr_valid)   , // write enable (qualified: wr_cs && wr_en && !full)
 .oe_0      (1'b0)       , // output enable
   
   
 .address_1 (rd_pointer) , // address_1 input
 .data_1    (data_ram)   , // data_1 bi-directional
 .cs_1      (rd_cs)      , // chip select
 .we_1      (1'b0)       , // Read enable
-.oe_1      (rd_en)        // output enable
+.oe_1      (rd_valid)     // output enable (qualified: rd_cs && rd_en && !empty)
 );
corrected_code:
ram_dp_ar_aw #(DATA_WIDTH,ADDR_WIDTH) DP_RAM (
  .clk     (clk),
.address_0 (wr_pointer) , // address_0 input
.data_0    (data_in)    , // data_0 bi-directional
.cs_0      (wr_cs)      , // chip select
.we_0      (wr_valid)   , // write enable (qualified: wr_cs && wr_en && !full)
.oe_0      (1'b0)       , // output enable


.address_1 (rd_pointer) , // address_1 input
.data_1    (data_ram)   , // data_1 bi-directional
.cs_1      (rd_cs)      , // chip select
.we_1      (1'b0)       , // Read enable
.oe_1      (rd_valid)     // output enable (qualified: rd_cs && rd_en && !empty)
);

assumptions: wr_valid and rd_valid, already declared in the module, correctly capture the intended write/read qualification (wr_cs&&wr_en&&!full and rd_cs&&rd_en&&!empty respectively) per REQ-002.

The dual-port RAM's write path is edge-triggered (per its documented behavior) and samples cs_0/we_0/address_0/data_0 once per clock edge, so gating we_0 with wr_valid does not introduce a new timing hazard.
status_cnt/pointer update logic itself (STATUS_COUNTER, WRITE_POINTER, READ_POINTER blocks) is spec-compliant as written; the defect is isolated to the RAM port connections.

The earliest two EMPTY FLAG FAIL entries (55ns/65ns, COUNT=1/2) may partly reflect a one-cycle registered-counter latency that is inherent and spec-compliant (REQ-012); this fix targets the data-corruption-driven failures (75/85/135/2765ns) for which strong code evidence exists.
limitations: This fix does not fully explain the very first two EMPTY FLAG FAIL events (55ns, 65ns) if they occur before any full-condition write could have occurred (RAM_DEPTH=256 by default); if those two failures are due to testbench sampling status flags before the one-cycle registered status_cnt update completes (a TB timing issue), this RTL patch will not resolve them and the TB timing model should be reviewed separately.

No waveform/internal signal trace of wr_pointer/rd_pointer/status_cnt/data_ram values was available to directly confirm RAM corruption versus a TB latency assumption; this fix is grounded in a real code-level inconsistency (unused qualifiers) rather than a directly observed internal RAM corruption trace.
Fix assumes RAM_DEPTH/ADDR_WIDTH defaults are unchanged and that ram_dp_ar_aw correctly implements synchronous write / async read semantics as documented in its header comment.
